hook: Every afternoon at a quarter past three, a little girl crosses Lorna’s road.

excerpt.text: Lorna Webb could tell the time by the street.

excerpt: She had done it for eleven years.
Here she stood still and the town came to her, three hundred children twice a day, and she knew them all.

excerpt.text: It was the only time in her life she had been able to stop anything just by standing still.

The girl with the fox walked beside her, and halfway across she looked up at Lorna, at the sign and then at Lorna’s face, and Lorna smiled at her, because that was what you did, and the girl didn’t smile back.
She just looked, the way children look at things they are trying to remember.

excerpt: Then she was on the far kerb.

excerpt.text: Someone was waiting for the girl.
She didn’t say anything to the girl. She didn’t bend down or ask how her day had been or take the rucksack the way mothers did.
Not at Lorna. Not at the school. At the corner by the bakery, from the far kerb, just once, quickly, as though checking that something was still there.

caption:
Every afternoon at a quarter past three, a little girl crosses Lorna Webb’s road.

For eleven years Lorna has known every child outside St Anne’s Primary. She doesn’t know this one.
